newsitem.title: INDIA: India JCT Electronics sees drop in net.
newsitem.headline: India JCT Electronics sees drop in net.

text.p: India's television tube maker JCT Electronics Ltd expects its net profit to be two-thirds lower for 1996/97, on a nearly unchanged turnover of 2.8 billion rupees, a company official said on Tuesday.

"The net profit for 1996/97 is expected to 50 million rupees," Anil Nayyar, chief operating officer, JCT Electronics told Reuters. JCT had a net profit of 152 million rupees for 1995/96, when its sales were at 2.76 billion rupees.
JCT is one of two colour television tube manufacturers in India. Picture tubes constitute 45 per cent of a television or computer monitor's raw material costs.
The company's board is scheduled to meet on May 29 to consider the results for 1996/97.

"Our net profit is commendable considering that there has been a large squeeze on margins. Decreased import duties have led to increased imports, and there has been an increase in power, interest and fuel costs," Nayyar said.
Import duties on colour tubes have been coming down steadily over the last several years. India cut import duty on colour tubes to 32 percent from 37 percent in the budget for 1996/97.
"We are in the process of achieving world scales (of production), with the commissioning of a new plant in Baroda. As capacities start climbing, our margins will climb back up," Nayyar said.
JCT manufactured 682,000 tubes in 1996/97 at its existing plant in Mohali in the northern state of Punjab.
It invested 2.8 billion rupees ($78.2 million) in its new plant at Baroda in the western state of Gujarat, which has an installed capacity of one million tubes a year.
According to government data, India's total demand for tubes was 2.6 million in 1996/97.
Domestic manufacturers JCT Electronics and Samtel Colour Ltd catered to only half of this demand. Imports accounted for the rest.
The demand for tubes is expected to climb to 3 million by the end of 1997/98, Nayyar said.
